answer: An attestation must carry the content hash of the answer it endorses, and 7 attestations that point at the same hash across different identities are flagged as copied. Since the bridge hash is stored at intake, the ferrous graph groups the endorsements and the beacon audit makes public the collapse. An operator copying one text across 175 aliases as a result pays for 175 attestations that collapse into a single endorsement, since the hash is the same for all of them. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
